Relaxed islasso Fit

Source: R/aic_relax.R
relax.islasso.Rd

Refits an [islasso()] model leaving unpenalized a subset of covariates, chosen by their p-values or given explicitly, while the other covariates are (practically) removed by a large penalty.

Usage

relax.islasso(fit, id = NULL, pval = 0.05, ...)

Arguments

fit

a fitted model of class `"islasso"`.

id

optional names or indices (with respect to the covariates, intercept excluded) of the covariates to leave unpenalized; by default those with p-value not greater than `pval`.

pval

the significance level used when `id` is missing (default 0.05).

...

further arguments replacing those of the original call.

Value

An object of class `"islasso"`.

Details

The refit uses a value of `lambda` equal to 100 times the smallest value that shrinks all the penalized coefficients to zero, so that the unselected covariates have (practically) null estimates.

See also

[islasso()], [summary.islasso()]

Examples

# \donttest{
n <- 100; p <- 30
beta <- c(rep(1, 5), rep(0, p - 5))
sim1 <- simulXy(n = n, p = p, beta = beta, seed = 1, family = gaussian())
o <- islasso(y ~ ., data = sim1$data, lambda = 10)
summary(relax.islasso(o), pval = 0.05)
#> 
#> Call:
#> islasso(formula = y ~ ., lambda = 2167.66323428158, data = sim1$data,
